enchant_guidance.label: Should Feral Druid Tank Choose Aldor or Scryer for BiS in TBC Classic Phase 1?
enchant_guidance.text: Unlike most other specs in TBC, the choice of Aldor versus Scryer faction has almost zero impact on the long-term PvE performance of a Feral Druid. For bear tanks, the only permanently relevant items provided by these factions are the two shoulder enchants for threat and avoidance, respectively. The Aldor threat enchant is , and the Scryer version is , both of which require Exalted reputation with the Aldor and Scryer factions, respectively. Despite providing different distributions of Attack Power versus Critical Strike Rating, calculations show that both enchants provide nearly identical TPS value within current modeling accuracy, so feel free to choose either faction based on personal preference.

enchant_guidance.label: Should Feral Druid Tank Choose Aldor or Scryer for BiS in TBC Classic Phase 1?
enchant_guidance.text: For mitigation, the Aldor faction offers  at Exalted reputation while the Scryers offer . Due to the way that Blizzard scaled rating stats in TBC, it turns out that 1 Defense Rating and 1 Dodge Rating provide an identical average reduction of DTPS (damage taken per second). So, just like the DPS enchants, the two enchant options provide the same average mitigation value, as they simply trade  5 Dodge Rotation for 5 Defense Rating. Furthermore, these avoidance enchants only become relevant from late Phase 3 onwards when the passive avoidance on feral gear is high enough to prioritize avoidance stacking. In a pre-raid setting, threat enchants provide a lot more overall tanking value, and this continues to be the case throughout Phase 1 and 2.
